text:
AcmeOps: Hey team — our webhook endpoint to https://hooks.acme.internal started returning 502/connection refused around 08:12 PST. Nothing changed on our side. Can you check if Redwood egress IPs changed for our Private VPC?
Lina: Sorry to hear that — sending to infra to verify. Can you paste a snippet of the failing request/headers if you have it?
AcmeOps: Here’s the curl output from our receiver logs: 
```
time=2026-03-12T08:12:23Z method=POST path=/webhook status=502 src_ip=10.0.2.45 dst_ip=34.120.55.2 error="connection refused"
```
Mike: I checked our webhook delivery logs for customer_id=acme-corp — I see retries at 08:12:20-08:14:10 and then a sharp drop. The source SNAT IP we used changed at 08:11:59 from 54.210.13.91 -> 34.120.55.2.
InfraBot: [automated] SNAT rotation executed for vpc-0a1b2c at 2026-03-12T08:11:59Z. New SNAT pool: 34.120.55.0/28.
AcmeOps: ugh — that’s likely it. Their firewall is IP allowlist only. They don’t accept the new SNAT. Can you confirm exact IPs to add?
Jamie: Confirmed from routing table: affected IPs are 34.120.55.2 and .3 (primary egress of that NAT gateway). We should give them the entire /28 so they don't need to update on every micro-rotation.
Sara: Quick note — we rotated SNAT to balance utilization in that AZ. This was planned but the customers in that VPC were not notified (ours was an internal rotation policy). We need to fix comms.
OpsOncall: Short-term mitigation: we can re-route Acme's webhooks via a stable egress path (reserved SNAT) or instruct them to add the /28. Which do you want?
AcmeOps: Adding the /28 is fastest on our side. Please provide the canonical list and the time window when it'll be in effect. Our security team needs expiry and audit details.
Mike: Canonical list: 34.120.55.0/28 (covers 34.120.55.1-14). This will be effective immediately and part of the current SNAT pool. We expect periodic rotations but not frequent /28 changes; we’ll flag upcoming rotations at least 24h in advance from now on.
AcmeOps: Also seeing DNS weirdness — some internal services saw the hostname still resolving to the old NAT DNS A record in their monitoring; could TTLs be contributing to a partial hit?
Lina: NAT addresses are not published in external DNS for customers, but if the customer has any internal resolver mappings or a cached IP-to-name association it could confuse their firewall logs. Recommend they clear any DNS caches and check security appliance logs for cached entries.
Jamie: Repro steps we ran: from a host in the same Private VPC, `curl -v https://hooks.acme.internal` returned connection refused when SNAT was not in allowlist, and accepted once we added /28. Traceroute shows SNAT change at jump 4.
AcmeOps: We added the /28 and deliveries resumed ~ 08:20. Thanks. Can you share the audit ticket and a remediation plan so our SOC signs off?
Mike: Filing follow-up ticket INC-2026-0342 for permanent fix and comms. Action items: (1) Add 24h rotation notification for affected Private VPCs, (2) offer reserved SNAT option to customers behind strict allowlists, (3) publish a short KB about clearing DNS caches and firewall rules.
Sara: Also adding a small runbook snippet for Support: how to verify SNAT change in delivery logs (`grep webhook | jq .src_snat`) and the quick mitigation (temporary reserved egress).
AcmeOps: Appreciate it. One last ask — can you add a note for our security team with the audit log slice showing the exact timestamps and IPs used?
Mike: Sent via secure share (s3 presigned link) with logs for 08:00–09:00 PST. Ping me if anything missing.
Lina: Closing loop here — customer confirmed success and will keep the /28 in their allowlist until we offer a reserved SNAT. Marking thread resolved unless anyone needs to add more. :white_check_mark:
